newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian airline passenger volume down in Jan, Feb.
newsitem.headline: Russian airline passenger volume down in Jan, Feb.

text.p: Russian airline passenger volume dropped in January and February from a year ago despite industry expectations of improvement, and airlines are in financial straits, a senior industry official said on Wednesday.

However Alexander Pleshakov, a board member of the Association of Russian Air Carriers and Transaero airline's chief executive, told Reuters he could not give a precise figure for the size of the decline.
He added that passenger volumes dropped 27 percent on Russian domestic routes in 1996 but increased 30 percent on international routes.
"Total passenger volume dropped 10 percent in 1996 compared with the previous year," he told Reuters.
Pleshakov said most Russian airlines were in deep crisis.
"There is a big gap between the profitability of the airlines and the companies which provide services for them, including airports," he said.
Pleshakov cited 30 percent profitability at airports, ticket selling agencies and airline fuelling companies last year compared to a four percent profitability among carriers.
But 70 percent of carriers are losing money, the Federal Aviation Service has said.

Pleshakov said only about three million Russians flew on commercial airlines' domestic flights in 1996. "That is a very low figure," he said, citing customer distrust of carriers as the main reason for the drop.
Russia, with a population of about 150 million, has also been hit by severe economic problems during economic reform.
The Federal Aviation Service said 118 of Russia's 328 Russian airlines lost their operating licences in 1996 and another 58 carriers could soon be on that list.
"This year may also be very difficult for Russian carriers," Pleshakov said.
Earlier this year the Aviation Service said that Russian airlines lost $220 million in 1996 and more than 100 carriers went out of business because fewer passengers could afford to fly than in 1995.
